solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A pure athletic run, making you feel better?

indicators.note: a stocking that has a run is unravelled, so these letters come apart and are rewoven

explanation.surface: A clean athletic jog leaves you feeling good, the clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like the jog in the surface but is the anagram signal on A PURE ATHLETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapeutical is an older form of therapeutic: having a healing or restorative effect.

clue.text: Angry nonsense upset fighters

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: sore can mean angry or aggrieved
rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Furious drivel upsets some warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SOREROT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Toreros are bullfighters, so they are a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Get rid of priest taking Mass, trendy troublemaker

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
M is the physics symbol for mass
in means fashionable, trendy
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A priest attending Mass alongside a fashionable agitator wants to be rid of something.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE, the Greek goddess of discord, is a crossword stock troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove it entirely, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Surprise: he uprooted a plant!

indicators.note: uprooted means pulled out, so the word he is pulled out of the exclamation

parts.note: Heavens! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in shock that a man has dug up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprise' stands for the exclamation HEAVENS, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Avens is a small flowering perennial of the rose family, also called herb bennet.

clue.text: Required hospital department (wasn't well)

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A patient needed the ear, nose and throat clinic because they felt poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: If something entailed effort, it necessitated it, so entailed means required.

clue.text: Row about 2p — this person being ungenerous?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the row is placed around the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
two Ps, written as 2p, also the price of a tiny coin

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a two-penny tip, suggesting a stingy customer.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip of 2p (two British pence) is mean, so the whole clue hints at a stingy giver of tips.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipper leaves gratuities; one leaving 2p is the miserly sort the question mark has in mind.

clue.text: Game involving a round trip — not one for drivers!

definitions.text: Game involving a round trip — not one for drivers!

parts.words: Game involving a round trip — not one for drivers!
parts.note: a lawn putting game played round a circle of numbered points, where golfers use only putters, never drivers

explanation.surface: A game with a circular course that motorists should avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' are golf clubs, not motorists; the round is a circle of twelve stations like a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock golf is putting from points set round a circle like the hours on a dial.

clue.text: Jumped into trench, keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the trench holds the other letter

parts.note: a leat is an open channel carrying water to a mill
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A soldier leapt silently into a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAT, a mill channel, is a British dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, to spring through the air.

clue.text: See pilot plunge finally into chasm

indicators.note: into places the last letter within the chasm word

parts.note: a gorge is a deep narrow valley or chasm

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word plunge

explanation.surface: Watch the pilot finally dive into a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' is not a person: George is slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George is airmen's slang for the autopilot that flies a plane unaided.

clue.text: Garment torn around end

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the torn word encloses the other

parts.note: rent means ripped, torn
an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing is ripped near its hem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garment torn' looks like an anagram of GARMENT; it is the definition, with RENT taking AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for clothing, so a garment is an item of it.

clue.text: Gas? Support an alternative ultimately

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word alternative

explanation.surface: Is gas a support, or an alternative fuel in the end?
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a hydrocarbon fuel gas, so it is an example of a gas.

clue.text: Journeys round India to find yesterday's buildings?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the journeys word goes round the letter

parts.note: runs are short trips or journeys
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Travellers tour India to see historic buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruins are the remains of old structures, buildings of the past.

clue.text: Sportsperson cries terribly, embracing girl

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the jumbled letters wrap round the girl
terribly means badly, so the letters of cries are put in bad order

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An athlete sobs badly while hugging a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cries' looks like the sportsperson's action, but 'terribly' scrambles it to ICESR, and 'embracing' places the girl inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-skater competes in a winter sport, so is a sportsperson.

clue.text: Crossword compiler includes a duck as water creature

indicators.note: includes means contains, so the compiler word holds the other letters

parts.note: a setter compiles crosswords
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter brings in a duck as an aquatic animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is not a bird: it is zero, O, from the cricket score.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea otter is a marine mammal of the Pacific, so a creature of the water.

clue.text: Saul of Tarsus as a vintner?

definitions.meaning: St Paul, born Saul of Tarsus
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, so a maker of tent is a vintner

explanation.surface: Was St Paul a wine merchant?
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red wine from Spain, used chiefly as communion wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's trade was making tents; read as tent plus maker it describes a winemaker.

clue.text: Power needed by cat to make sudden attack

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
the ounce is the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A cat needs strength to leap on prey.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to spring suddenly on prey or a victim, an abrupt assault.

clue.text: Hear horseman come a cropper when darkness descends

indicators.note: hear says the horseman word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a knight is a mounted soldier
come a cropper is an idiom for having a heavy fall

explanation.surface: Listen to a rider tumble from his horse as dark falls.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT spoken gives NIGHT. 'Come a cropper' is British slang for a bad fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the time at which darkness comes.

clue.text: Woodworker's initial actions ruined good-quality oak

indicators.note: initial takes the first letter of the word Woodworker's
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of actions are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A carpenter's first moves spoiled fine oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns ACTIONS into AINSCOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot originally meant fine imported oak boarding, later the oak panelling made from it.

clue.text: Appearing to be heartless — should be showing understanding

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: seeming means appearing to be

explanation.surface: Someone who looks cold ought to show sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the M at the centre of SEEMING.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to understand, as in 'I see', so seeing means comprehending.

clue.text: Render in a flexible manner

definitions.meaning: the adverb of supple, meaning pliantly

explanation.walkthrough: The adverb is pronounced SUP-lee, from supple, unlike the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying is giving or rendering; supply as an adverb means in a supple, bendable way.

clue.text: One queen at war with another?

definitions.text: One queen at war with another?

parts.words: One queen at war with another?
parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so two queens battling is a scrap between cats

explanation.surface: A monarch wages war on a rival monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' means a female cat, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A catfight is a fight between cats, and colloquially a vicious quarrel.

clue.text: Provider of milk — right always for waiter to bring?

parts.note: a teat is a nipple that gives milk
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Milk and the right things are always for a waiter to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea tray is the flat platter on which a waiter carries the cups and pot.

clue.text: Lizard in South American region, one climbing up

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing up means moving higher in the column, to the front

parts.note: Guiana is the region in the north-east of South America
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lizard lives in a South American region, one climbing up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing up' lifts the I of GUIANA to the top of the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

clue.text: Tramping around to ensnare a bird

indicators.note: ensnare means trap inside, so the jumbled letters close round the letter
around here means scattered about, signalling the letters of Tramping are rearranged

explanation.surface: A walker roaming about tries to trap a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns TRAMPING into PTRMIGN, which 'to ensnare' wraps round A.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions, so a game bird.

clue.text: Singers needing some signal to start

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Choir members need a cue to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition 'Singers needing' was changed to 'Singers': 'needing' only links the definition to the wordplay, and the answer means singers, not singers needing.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos sing the lower female or high male part in a choir.

clue.text: That bread is mine, thank you!

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone claims a loaf: that one's mine, thanks!
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow Middle Eastern loaf, a type of bread.

clue.text: Old city's president presented with timeless garment

indicators.note: timeless removes the letter standing for time, T

parts.note: a tunic is a loose garment

explanation.surface: A president is given a classic, ageless robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic means belonging to ancient Carthage, so describes that old city's people and wars.

clue.text: Tobacco and port

explanation.definitionFit: The Syrian harbour city gave its name to the strong cured leaf exported through it.

clue.text: Fellow Arab?

parts.note: a fellow is a man and an Arab is a breed of horse, so a man-horse creature

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is the horse breed, not a person; together with 'Fellow' it pictures half man, half horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur of Greek myth has a man's upper body on a horse's body.

clue.text: Classic lay art slammed in withering tones?

indicators.note: slammed means battered, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Critics savaged traditional amateur painting with scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking sarcastically means using cutting, mocking irony, the tone of withering remarks.
